name: TLS client certificates
plain: A site can ask the browser to present a certificate stored on the computer.
meaning: Certificates identify a person or company. The browser asks which cert to send; used in banks and enterprise.

web.api: TLS CertificateRequest during handshake; browser certificate chooser

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: A site can ask the browser to present a certificate stored on the computer.

limits.headline: Can ask your browser to show a certificate stored on your computer
limits.user_action: You open a bank or company site and pick a certificate in the box that appears
can: Ask you to choose one certificate from those on your device
Receive the certificate you choose to prove who you or your company are
Sign you in to a bank or work site without a password
cannot: Pick a certificate for you without your choice, unless you set the browser to auto choose
Get the private key; it stays on your device or security card
See certificates you did not choose to send

story.what_it_is: The browser can offer a digital ID card stored on your computer when a site asks.
story.for_you: A box may pop up asking which certificate to use, or it picks one for you. There is no password box. You mostly see this at work, school or a government service.
story.for_makers: Makers use client certificates for very strong machine and person checks, such as a bank or an internal company tool. It proves the device is one the company issued before the site loads.

use_cases.example: A company intranet only opens on laptops that carry a certificate from IT, so a stolen password alone does not get in.
A business bank portal asks for a certificate stored on a smart card or token before it shows balances.
A government tax or health web service uses a national ID certificate to prove who is filing.
An engineer reaches a staging server or code tool that only accepts browsers with the right certificate.
An online gaming tournament admin panel is limited to organizer laptops with certificates, so only staff can change brackets.
A security team logs which certificate connected to spot an unusual device.

risks: Hard to set up and move

abuse: Identity linking across sites if the same cert is used

history.change: Client cert support from early TLS
